image: So the noble one is together,
lines: Regret gone.
If a horse is lost, do not chase it —
it comes back by itself.
Meeting bad people: no harm.
He meets the lord in a lane.
No harm.
He sees a cart dragged back,
its ox pulled up short,
and the man branded, his nose cut off.
There is no beginning, but there is an end.
Estranged and alone,
he meets the first husband.
They exchange trust: danger, but no harm.
Regret gone.
His kin bite through the skin.
Going: what harm?
Estranged and alone, he sees a pig carrying dirt, and a cartload of ghosts.
First he draws his bow on them, then he lays the bow down.
They are not raiders, but suitors.
If he goes and meets rain: good.

notes.name_en: 睽 is eyes turned apart, estrangement; 'Estranged', not Wilhelm's 'Opposition'.
notes.L3: 天且劓: 天 read as forehead-branding (黥), 劓 nose-cutting — a punished man, kept concrete.
notes.L6: The suitors refrain (3 L2) kept in the same words; ghosts were the marriage party mis-seen. 先張之弧後說之弧: B gives the bow its archer ('he draws… he lays').
